summary: Targeted LDP sessions can be started by a router for many reasons, but until now the router receiving the request had no way to know why and so could not decide whether to accept it. This document defines a way for a router to advertise which targeted applications it is willing to accept sessions for, so unwanted sessions can be refused.

eli5.summary: Imagine a door that anyone can knock on. This lets the house post a sign saying which kinds of visitors are welcome, so it can politely turn the rest away.

questions: how does a router limit which targeted ldp sessions it accepts
what is the targeted application capability
how does ldp reject a tldp session
what is a ta-id in ldp
subtitle: A way for a router to say which targeted LDP applications a session is for, so the other side can accept or refuse it.

tldr.problem: Some applications, such as remote Loop-Free Alternates and BGP auto-discovered pseudowires, automatically start targeted LDP sessions with any router. The router on the receiving end has no information about the application, so it cannot decide whether to accept the session.
tldr.mechanism: Each side lists its Targeted Application Capability (TAC) in the LDP Initialization message. The session goes ahead only if the two lists share at least one application, and only label bindings for the negotiated applications are exchanged.
tldr.outcome: A responding router can limit sessions per application, and sessions carry only the FEC label bindings they need. The RFC updates RFC 7473 and is a Proposed Standard.

today: RFC 8223 is a Proposed Standard published in August 2017. It updates RFC 7473 and has not been obsoleted or updated by another RFC.

sections.title: The Problem With Targeted LDP Sessions
sections.content:
LDP uses Extended Discovery to set up a targeted LDP (tLDP) adjacency and then a session. A Label Switching Router (LSR) starts it by sending a tLDP Hello to a specific address. The remote LSR accepts or ignores that Hello based on local configuration only.

For something like a FEC 128 pseudowire, the remote LSR is configured with the source address, so this works. But remote Loop-Free Alternates (LFAs) and BGP auto-discovered pseudowires start sessions automatically to any LSR, based on local state. The remote LSR is not configured with the source, so it either answers every tLDP Hello or ignores them all.

The initiating LSR can limit how many automatic sessions it starts per application. The responding LSR has no such information, so it cannot apply a similar limit to incoming sessions, and it does not know whether the session is for configured applications, automatic ones or both.
sections.eli5: A house with an open door can not tell who is coming or why. It either lets everyone in or ignores every knock.

sections.title: The Targeted Application Capability
sections.content:
The Targeted Application Capability (TAC) is a capability TLV, advertised as defined in RFC 5561. The U flag MUST be set to 1, so a router that does not know the capability silently ignores it. The IANA code point for the TLV is 0x050F.

The capability data is a list of Targeted Application Elements (TAEs). Each element has a 16-bit Targeted Application Identifier (TA-Id) and an E (enable) bit. An E bit of 1 advertises the application and 0 withdraws it.

The identifiers live in a new IANA registry. Examples are 0x0001 for LDPv4 Tunneling, 0x0004 for LDPv4 Remote LFA, 0x0006 for LDP FEC 128 PW and 0x0007 for LDP FEC 129 PW.
sections.eli5: The sign on the door is a list of reasons for visiting, each with its own number. Each item can be switched on or off.

sections.title: Negotiating Applications at Session Setup
sections.content:
An LSR MAY put a TAC TLV in the LDP Initialization message, listing zero or more TAEs. If the same TA-Id appears twice, the receiver processes the first and ignores the duplicates. An unknown TA-Id is silently ignored. If the TAC TLV is missing or not understood, negotiation is considered unsuccessful and the session is set up as in RFC 5036.

On receiving a valid TAC TLV, an LSR MUST send its own list of the TA-Ids it supports. If the two lists have at least one TAE in common, the session proceeds. If not, the LSR MUST send a Session Rejected/Targeted Application Capability Mismatch Notification and close the session.

After rejection, an LSR that was the active side in session setup must either close the session and tear down the tLDP adjacency (initiator only) or set its session setup retry interval to the maximum value, 0xFFFF. It clears the backoff when it detects a configuration change that touches the TAC TLV. By default an LSR SHOULD accept tLDP Hellos and decide on the session once it sees the application information, and SHOULD let operators configure any TA-Id, including private ones.

Only the negotiated applications count. If the initiator offers A, B and C and the responder offers C, D and E, the result is C. If the responder offers D and E only, the result is none and the session is refused.
sections.eli5: Both sides show their list of reasons. If at least one reason matches, the visit goes ahead. If nothing matches, the door stays shut.

sections.title: Mapping Applications to FEC Label Bindings
sections.content:
After a session is set up using the TAC, both LSRs MUST distribute FEC label bindings for the negotiated applications only. An LSR in downstream on-demand mode MUST also request bindings for the negotiated applications only. For a BGP auto-discovered pseudowire, for example, only FEC 129 label bindings are distributed.

To make this work, each application is mapped to LDP FEC element types. LDPv4 Tunneling and LDPv4 Remote LFA map to IPv4 prefix FECs, LDP FEC 128 PW maps to the PWid FEC element, and LDP FEC 129 PW maps to the Generalized PWid FEC element. mLDP Tunneling maps to the P2MP, MP2MP-up, MP2MP-down, HSMP-downstream and HSMP-upstream types.

If both sides also negotiated the Dynamic Capability, the TAC can be renegotiated later with a Capability message that carries an incremental update. Elements with the E bit set to 1 add an application and elements with 0 withdraw one. This can add or withdraw label bindings, or lead to teardown of the adjacency and session. If no common element remains, the LSR sends the mismatch Notification and closes the session.
sections.eli5: Once the visit is agreed, the guests only bring the things that fit that reason, not everything they own.

sections.title: Working Alongside State Advertisement Control
sections.content:
RFC 7473 defines the State Advertisement Control (SAC) TLV, with which a speaker says it is or is not interested in receiving state for an application. The TAC negotiation is symmetric: both peers advertise state for the same applications. SAC can then make this asymmetric.

The RFC says TAC should be used when the responder does not know about targeted applications (remote LFAs, BGP auto-discovered pseudowires), and SAC when it does (FEC 128 pseudowire). When both are used on one session, TAC takes precedence for enabling: peers MUST NOT advertise state for an application that was not negotiated, even if a SAC TLV asks for it. SAC takes precedence for disabling: if a speaker said it is not interested, the peer MUST NOT send that state, even for a negotiated application.

The RFC also lists the mappings from targeted applications to the application state of RFC 7473, such as LDPv4 Remote LFA to IPv4 Prefix-LSPs and LDP FEC 129 PW to FEC 129 P2P-PW.
sections.eli5: The guest list says who may come in. A second note can say "please do not send me that one", and that note always wins when it asks for less.

sections.title: Use Cases
sections.content:
The RFC walks through four cases. For an automatic remote LFA session, the initiator sends an Initialization message with a remote LFA TAE. The receiver checks that it is configured to accept remote LFA sessions and that the configured limit is not exceeded, and may then reply with its own TAC.

For a FEC 129 auto-discovery session, a service provider can limit how many auto-discovered sessions a border LSR accepts, and the receiver can apply a policy such as accepting only from a list of source addresses.

When a sender offers both LDP-over-RSVP tunneling and remote LFA, a receiver that has reached its remote LFA limit can still form the session for the tunneling application, because both need the same FECs. For mLDP node protection, a Merge Point LSR can ask the upstream point of local repair for a session, and the PLR accepts it if it is configured for this and no limit is exceeded.
sections.eli5: The house can say yes to the plumber but no to a seventh salesperson, because it knows why each one knocked.

sections.title: Security and IANA Considerations
sections.content:
The RFC says it does not change the LDP security considerations of RFC 5036. DoS attacks through Extended Hellos can still be handled by filtering them with access lists, and an LSR can accept auto-discovered Extended Hellos only from a configured list of source addresses. Once both sides support the TAC, a session is established only after the TAC negotiation succeeds, and each side MUST advertise only the TA-Ids it is configured to support.

IANA assigned TLV code point 0x050F and status code 0x0000004C, and created the "LDP Targeted Application Identifier" registry with range 0x0001 to 0xFFFE. Values 0x0001 to 0x1FFF need IETF Review and 0x2000 to 0xF7FF are First Come First Served. Values 0xF800 to 0xFBFF are for private use and 0xFC00 to 0xFFFE for experimental use.
sections.eli5: The new sign does not give strangers any new keys, and the house still checks who may knock at all.
